treatments.label: Quiet Editorial Studio
treatments.signature: tonal canvas, one authored graphic device, restrained type contrast, and an object-led reading rhythm
treatments.palette: Use an off-white or ink-toned canvas with one owned accent and visible hairline rules; choose the temperature from real content and never default to beige or a rainbow accent set.
treatments.typography: Use one dependable UI/body face plus one earned display role for a short title or section marker; keep body measure readable and use explicit line breaks instead of oversized type.
treatments.composition: Use a 12-column asymmetric grid, a narrow index or caption rail, one dominant content/object field, and a visible next chapter; let one edge repeat across sections.
treatments.material: Build depth from canvas, object surface, rule, crop, and one active tone; keep radius and shadow vocabulary small so the page feels authored rather than decorated.
treatments.signatureDevice: Choose one repeatable device such as a numbered index, hairline rule, cropped color field, oversized section marker, or offset caption; repeat it with restraint.
treatments.assetStrategy: Use real target media when it carries meaning. If the domain object is unknown, make a complete typographic/graphic composition or generate a target-specific asset; never use a generic stock hero as identity.
treatments.expressionBudget: medium-high: one clear visual thesis and one repeatable device, not a pile of effects
antiAiChecks: No centered slogan floating over an empty background.
No beige editorial skin without a content or material reason.
No three-card feature row used as the page's only structure.
No second display face, effect, or accent added without a named job.
No abstract brand adjectives standing in for a real subject or action.
renderChecks: The page has a recognizable silhouette in grayscale and at thumbnail size.
The signature device appears consistently without becoming decoration.
The first viewport identifies the subject before the visual style is admired.
Desktop and mobile preserve the same thesis through deliberate restaging.

treatments.label: Material Object Studio
treatments.signature: material contrast and object continuity carry the identity while copy and proof stay practical
treatments.palette: Use studio neutrals or a target-owned dark/light contrast; let the object's finish provide color and reserve the accent for action or state.
treatments.typography: Pair quiet utility type with one short product/chapter role; specs and controls remain compact and measurable.
treatments.composition: Give the object a stable stage, offset the copy/action rail, and change crop or scale between chapters instead of repeating a 50/50 split.
treatments.material: Use crop, edge, reflection, tonal field, and object detail as depth; avoid floating-card theater and unearned glass.
treatments.signatureDevice: One material cue or object detail repeats across the page: edge highlight, macro crop, finish swatch, measured rule, or controlled shadow.
treatments.assetStrategy: Use official/authorized or target-specific product media; a static object, poster, or specification path must survive missing media and reduced motion.
treatments.expressionBudget: high only when the object and proof are real; otherwise medium and information-led
antiAiChecks: No fake product render presented as evidence.
No repeated image-left/text-right chapter template.
No luxury palette without material or performance proof.
No scroll choreography hiding specs, compatibility, or action.
renderChecks: Object silhouette and focal crop remain legible at mobile width.
At least three chapters change composition, crop, or scale.
The practical decision path works with motion and color removed.

treatments.label: Warm Humanist Editorial
treatments.signature: human-scale type, specific reassurance, and tactile structure without turning the surface childish
treatments.palette: Use a warm but high-contrast canvas with one grounded accent; keep warmth in material and copy, not in low-contrast beige wash.
treatments.typography: Use a humanist body face with comfortable line-height and a restrained title role; keep labels conversational but precise.
treatments.composition: Use a clear reading edge, generous but purposeful sections, real people/content early, and a strong action near the relevant story or task.
treatments.material: Use paper-like tonal shifts, rules, soft image crops, and tactile control states; avoid childish blobs and decorative illustration filler.
treatments.signatureDevice: A recurring reassurance marker, editorial caption, hand-sized control, or human quote fragment gives the surface character.
treatments.assetStrategy: Use real people, places, work, or target-specific illustrations; do not use generic lifestyle stock to fake trust.
treatments.expressionBudget: medium: warm, specific, and tactile without losing contrast or task speed
antiAiChecks: No beige-only palette with weak contrast.
No generic friendly adjectives without a concrete reassurance.
No decorative illustration replacing the real person, task, or outcome.
No oversized playful type in a high-frequency workflow.
renderChecks: The subject and next action remain clear in grayscale.
Text, controls, and image crops remain comfortable on mobile.
Warmth survives without relying on low contrast or motion.

treatments.label: Ink State Instrument
treatments.signature: ink, rules, and state markers make the active object feel like an instrument rather than a card dashboard
treatments.palette: Use ink or restrained neutral surfaces with one semantic/action accent; every state also gets text, position, or shape support.
treatments.typography: Use a compact UI face, optional mono for traces/IDs, and no display role in the chrome; hierarchy comes from weight, alignment, and state.
treatments.composition: Keep a live work object, rail/timeline, and next action on one stable axis; collapse the rail deliberately on mobile.
treatments.material: Use dividers, selected rows, tonal surfaces, and focus rings before glow or glass; stable geometry matters more than atmosphere.
treatments.signatureDevice: A state rail, timeline marker, status strip, or selected-object highlight repeats through the workflow.
treatments.assetStrategy: Use the live process, trace, media object, or deterministic state as the visual material; do not fabricate a cinematic hero around an empty workflow.
treatments.expressionBudget: medium: authored through state choreography and geometry, not decorative effects
antiAiChecks: No glowing AI orb or generic chat shell.
No dashboard tile wall before the work object.
No status communicated only by color or animation.
No dark mode chosen only to look technical.
renderChecks: A user can explain the current state without motion.
Selected, waiting, success, and error states differ structurally.
Rail, object, and action remain reachable at mobile width.

treatments.label: Data Graphic Clarity
treatments.signature: a strict information grid with one restrained graphic accent makes comparison feel designed rather than decorated
treatments.palette: Use a quiet canvas, one analytical accent, and semantic colors only where the data model earns them; preserve grayscale legibility.
treatments.typography: Use aligned tabular numbers, compact labels, and a readable explanatory measure; no display headline before the data relationship.
treatments.composition: Put filter/context above the dominant table, chart, map, or detail relationship; use selected rows and open work surfaces instead of metric cards.
treatments.material: Use dividers, tonal bands, selection treatment, and precise column rhythm; avoid chart glow and rainbow decoration.
treatments.signatureDevice: A consistent data cursor, selected-row rule, unit marker, or comparison band gives the surface a visual identity.
treatments.assetStrategy: The data relationship is the primary visual; use realistic units, freshness, partial states, and meaningful sample values.
treatments.expressionBudget: medium-low: visual character comes from precision and comparison, not spectacle
antiAiChecks: No four-KPI preamble by default.
No rainbow chart palette without a data model.
No chart detached from table/detail context.
No tiny gray labels as the only explanation.
renderChecks: Numbers, units, long labels, and selected context do not collide.
The hierarchy survives grayscale and reduced contrast.
Partial, stale, and empty states retain the same composition.

treatments.label: Specimen Graphic System
treatments.signature: stable preview frames and a quiet index let the working specimen provide the visual interest
treatments.palette: Use a restrained canvas and let each specimen own its internal color; page chrome should not compete with the demo.
treatments.typography: Use a clear specimen title, compact metadata, and restrained mono for code/props; avoid marketing copy before the first working example.
treatments.composition: Use index + strong specimen + visible next example; only use a grid when comparison is genuinely the job.
treatments.material: Preview frame contrast and stable geometry carry the system; avoid wrapping every demo in another decorative card.
treatments.signatureDevice: A consistent frame header, index marker, or install/action rail repeats across specimens.
treatments.assetStrategy: Use working components and realistic states; never use screenshots or copied demo filler as the primary proof.
treatments.expressionBudget: medium: the specimen behavior is the expression
antiAiChecks: No unrelated effect collage.
No identical demo cards with only headings changed.
No dark-glow source skin inherited by default.
No hero copy before the first working specimen.
renderChecks: The specimen is legible before the caption is read.
Frames remain stable while states change.
At least one specimen shows a non-default state.
